policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders 'the chief of the thirty,' which distinguishes ketiv השלושים from qere השלישים; the mapped textual-variant note gives 'captains' as the other reading.
ASV 'David longed' does not distinguish the qere ויתאיו from the ketiv ויתאו, and no mapped textual note decides between them; retain the documented base fallback.
ASV 'and had a name among the three' renders qere ולו ('and to him') and distinguishes it from ketiv ולא ('and not'); the Hebrew-gloss notes concern names and 'slain,' not this unit.
ASV names 'Jeiel,' distinguishing qere ויעיאל from ketiv ויעואל; no mapped note supplies contrary textual evidence.
